byte 1	MQTT Control Packet type (1)	Reserved
	0	0	0	1	0	0	0	0
requirements.condition: For a CONNECT Control Packet
requirements.required_behavior: Bits 7 through 4 of fixed-header byte 1 must encode MQTT Control Packet type 1 as 0001.
requirements.why_checkable: The high nibble of the first received or emitted CONNECT byte can be compared with 0001.

requirements.quote:

byte 1	MQTT Control Packet type (1)	Reserved
	0	0	0	1	0	0	0	0
requirements.condition: For a CONNECT Control Packet
requirements.required_behavior: Reserved bits 3 through 0 of fixed-header byte 1 must be 0000.
requirements.why_checkable: The low nibble of the first CONNECT byte can be masked and compared with zero.

requirements.quote: byte 2…	Remaining Length
requirements.condition: For a CONNECT Control Packet
requirements.required_behavior: The Remaining Length field must begin at fixed-header byte 2 and may occupy subsequent bytes according to its encoding.
requirements.why_checkable: A decoder can assert the starting byte of the Remaining Length field in the fixed header.

requirements.quote: Remaining Length is the length of the variable header (10 bytes) plus the length of the Payload.
requirements.condition: For a CONNECT Control Packet
requirements.required_behavior: Remaining Length must equal 10 plus the CONNECT Payload length in bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded Remaining Length can be compared with the fixed ten-byte variable header plus the observed Payload byte count.

requirements.quote: It is encoded in the manner described in section 2.2.3.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the CONNECT Remaining Length field
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation would use the Remaining Length encoding defined by section 2.2.3.
requirements.why_checkable: The referenced encoding algorithm is not present in this chunk, so this sentence alone does not supply complete expected bytes or acceptance boundaries.

requirements.quote: The variable header for the CONNECT Packet consists of four fields in the following order:  Protocol Name, Protocol Level, Connect Flags, and Keep Alive.
requirements.condition: For the variable header of a CONNECT Packet
requirements.required_behavior: Protocol Name must be the first field.
requirements.why_checkable: The first decoded variable-header field can be identified and compared with Protocol Name.

requirements.quote: The variable header for the CONNECT Packet consists of four fields in the following order:  Protocol Name, Protocol Level, Connect Flags, and Keep Alive.
requirements.condition: For the variable header of a CONNECT Packet
requirements.required_behavior: Protocol Level must be the second field, immediately after Protocol Name.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded field sequence can be checked at the Protocol Name-to-Protocol Level boundary.

requirements.quote: The variable header for the CONNECT Packet consists of four fields in the following order:  Protocol Name, Protocol Level, Connect Flags, and Keep Alive.
requirements.condition: For the variable header of a CONNECT Packet
requirements.required_behavior: Connect Flags must be the third field, immediately after Protocol Level.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded field sequence can be checked at the Protocol Level-to-Connect Flags boundary.

requirements.quote: The variable header for the CONNECT Packet consists of four fields in the following order:  Protocol Name, Protocol Level, Connect Flags, and Keep Alive.
requirements.condition: For the variable header of a CONNECT Packet
requirements.required_behavior: Keep Alive must be the fourth and final field, immediately after Connect Flags.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The variable header must not contain another field after Keep Alive.
requirements.why_checkable: The final decoded variable-header field and the end boundary of the ten-byte header can be asserted.

requirements.quote:
Protocol Name
byte 1	Length MSB (0)	0	0	0	0	0	0	0	0
byte 2	Length LSB (4)	0	0	0	0	0	1	0	0
requirements.condition: For the Protocol Name field in a CONNECT variable header
requirements.required_behavior: The two-byte string-length prefix must be 0x0004, with MSB 0 and LSB 4.
requirements.why_checkable: The first two Protocol Name bytes can be compared directly with 0x00 and 0x04.

requirements.quote: The Protocol Name is a UTF-8 encoded string that represents the protocol name “MQTT”, capitalized as shown.
requirements.condition: For the Protocol Name field in a CONNECT Packet
requirements.required_behavior: The field must use the MQTT UTF-8 encoded-string representation.
requirements.why_checkable: A decoder can validate the field's UTF-8 string representation and length prefix.

requirements.quote: The Protocol Name is a UTF-8 encoded string that represents the protocol name “MQTT”, capitalized as shown.
requirements.condition: For the Protocol Name field in a CONNECT Packet
requirements.required_behavior: The decoded value must be exactly the case-sensitive string “MQTT”.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not treat a differently capitalized value as the MQTT 3.1.1 Protocol Name.
requirements.why_checkable: The four decoded characters can be compared exactly with uppercase M, Q, T, T.

requirements.quote: If the protocol name is incorrect the Server MAY disconnect the Client, or it MAY continue processing the CONNECT packet in accordance with some other specification. In the latter case, the Server MUST NOT continue to process the CONNECT packet in line with this specification [MQTT-3.1.2-1].
requirements.condition: When a Server receives a CONNECT Packet with an incorrect Protocol Name
requirements.required_behavior: The Server may disconnect the Client or may continue processing only in accordance with another specification.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: If the Server continues processing, it must not process that CONNECT Packet as MQTT under this specification.
requirements.error_behavior: Disconnect the Client, or route processing to another applicable specification without continuing under MQTT 3.1.1.
requirements.why_checkable: An incorrect-name CONNECT Packet can be injected and the connection and selected protocol-processing path observed.

requirements.quote: The 8 bit unsigned value that represents the revision level of the protocol used by the Client.
requirements.condition: For the Protocol Level field in a CONNECT Packet
requirements.required_behavior: The field must be represented as an 8-bit unsigned value.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and unsigned interpretation can be checked during packet decoding.

requirements.quote: The value of the Protocol Level field for the version 3.1.1 of the protocol is 4 (0x04).
requirements.condition: When a Client identifies MQTT version 3.1.1 in CONNECT
requirements.required_behavior: The Protocol Level field must equal 4 (0x04).
requirements.why_checkable: The single Protocol Level byte can be compared directly with 0x04.

requirements.quote: byte 7	Level(4)	0	0	0	0	0	1	0	0
requirements.condition: For a CONNECT variable header
requirements.required_behavior: Protocol Level must occupy variable-header byte 7.
requirements.why_checkable: The Protocol Level byte offset can be checked against the start of the variable header.

requirements.quote: The Server MUST respond to the CONNECT Packet with a CONNACK return code 0x01 (unacceptable protocol level) and then disconnect the Client if the Protocol Level is not supported by the Server [MQTT-3.1.2-2].
requirements.condition: When the received Protocol Level is not supported by the Server
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must send a CONNACK Packet whose return code is 0x01 (unacceptable protocol level).
requirements.error_behavior: Return CONNACK code 0x01 before closing the connection.
requirements.why_checkable: An unsupported level can be sent and the response packet type and return code decoded.

requirements.quote: The Server MUST respond to the CONNECT Packet with a CONNACK return code 0x01 (unacceptable protocol level) and then disconnect the Client if the Protocol Level is not supported by the Server [MQTT-3.1.2-2].
requirements.condition: After the Server sends CONNACK return code 0x01 for an unsupported Protocol Level
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must disconnect the Client after sending the CONNACK response.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Server must not keep the MQTT Network Connection open after that response.
requirements.error_behavior: Close the Network Connection after the error CONNACK.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet order and subsequent connection closure can be observed on an unsupported-level test.

requirements.required_behavior: The Connect Flags field must occupy variable-header byte 8.
requirements.why_checkable: The field byte offset can be checked against the start of the CONNECT variable header.

requirements.required_behavior: Bit 2 must encode Will Flag.
requirements.why_checkable: A bit-mask check can confirm the Will Flag field occupies bit 2.

requirements.quote: Position: bit 1 of the Connect Flags byte.
requirements.condition: For the CONNECT Connect Flags byte
requirements.required_behavior: Clean Session must occupy bit 1.
requirements.why_checkable: A bit-mask check can confirm the Clean Session field occupies bit 1.

requirements.quote: The Server MUST validate that the reserved flag in the CONNECT Control Packet is set to zero and disconnect the Client if it is not zero [MQTT-3.1.2-3].
requirements.condition: When the Server validates a CONNECT Control Packet
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must validate that reserved bit 0 of the Connect Flags byte is zero.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can independently set and clear Connect Flags bit 0 and observe validation outcomes.

requirements.quote: The Server MUST validate that the reserved flag in the CONNECT Control Packet is set to zero and disconnect the Client if it is not zero [MQTT-3.1.2-3].
requirements.condition: When reserved bit 0 of the received CONNECT Connect Flags byte is nonzero
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must disconnect the Client.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Server must not continue the MQTT connection after detecting the nonzero reserved bit.
requirements.why_checkable: A malformed CONNECT with bit 0 set can be injected and connection closure observed.

requirements.quote: If CleanSession is set to 0, the Server MUST resume communications with the Client based on state from the current Session (as identified by the Client identifier).
requirements.condition: When CleanSession is 0 and a current Session exists for the Client
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must resume communications using state from that current Session.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Server must not discard the existing Session and unconditionally start without its state.
requirements.why_checkable: Stored state can be prepared before disconnection and its reuse observed after a CleanSession=0 reconnect.

requirements.quote: If CleanSession is set to 0, the Server MUST resume communications with the Client based on state from the current Session (as identified by the Client identifier).
requirements.condition: When selecting a current Session for a CONNECT with CleanSession set to 0
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must identify the current Session by the Client identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Server must not resume a Session belonging to a different Client identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: Reconnects using distinct Client identifiers can verify that stored state is selected by identifier without cross-client leakage.

requirements.quote: If there is no Session associated with the Client identifier the Server MUST create a new Session.
requirements.condition: When CleanSession is 0 and no Session is associated with the Client identifier
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must create a new Session for that Client identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: A previously unseen Client identifier can connect with CleanSession=0 and resulting Session creation can be observed.

requirements.quote: The Client and Server MUST store the Session after the Client and Server are disconnected [MQTT-3.1.2-4].
requirements.condition: After disconnection of a Session established with CleanSession set to 0
requirements.required_behavior: The Client must store its Session state after disconnection.
requirements.why_checkable: Client-side protocol state can be created, disconnected, and checked for persistence.

requirements.quote: The Client and Server MUST store the Session after the Client and Server are disconnected [MQTT-3.1.2-4].
requirements.condition: After disconnection of a Session established with CleanSession set to 0
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must store its Session state after disconnection.
requirements.why_checkable: Server-side protocol state can be created, disconnected, and checked for persistence on reconnect.

requirements.quote: After the disconnection of a Session that had CleanSession set to 0, the Server MUST store further QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages that match any subscriptions that the client had at the time of disconnection as part of the Session state [MQTT-3.1.2-5].
requirements.condition: After a CleanSession=0 Session disconnects, when a further QoS 1 message matches a Subscription the Client had at disconnection
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must store the QoS 1 message as part of that Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: A QoS 1 matching publication can be issued while the Client is disconnected and recovered on reconnect.

requirements.quote: After the disconnection of a Session that had CleanSession set to 0, the Server MUST store further QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages that match any subscriptions that the client had at the time of disconnection as part of the Session state [MQTT-3.1.2-5].
requirements.condition: After a CleanSession=0 Session disconnects, when a further QoS 2 message matches a Subscription the Client had at disconnection
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must store the QoS 2 message as part of that Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: A QoS 2 matching publication can be issued while the Client is disconnected and recovered on reconnect.

requirements.quote: It MAY also store QoS 0 messages that meet the same criteria.
requirements.condition: If the Server elects to store QoS 0 messages for a disconnected CleanSession=0 Session
requirements.required_behavior: The stored QoS 0 messages may be those that match Subscriptions the Client had at disconnection and may be included in Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: For an implementation that enables optional QoS 0 persistence, matching publications can be distinguished from nonmatching publications and Session contents inspected.

requirements.quote: If CleanSession is set to 1, the Client and Server MUST discard any previous Session and start a new one.
requirements.condition: When the Client connects with CleanSession set to 1
requirements.required_behavior: The Client must discard any previous Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: Existing Client state can be prepared and checked after a CleanSession=1 connection.

requirements.quote: If CleanSession is set to 1, the Client and Server MUST discard any previous Session and start a new one.
requirements.condition: When the Server receives CONNECT with CleanSession set to 1
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must discard any previous Session for the Client.
requirements.why_checkable: Existing Server-side Session state can be prepared and checked after a CleanSession=1 connection.

requirements.quote: If CleanSession is set to 1, the Client and Server MUST discard any previous Session and start a new one.
requirements.condition: When CleanSession is set to 1
requirements.required_behavior: The Client and Server must start a new Session after discarding the previous Session.
requirements.why_checkable: New Session creation and absence of prior state can be observed after connection establishment.

requirements.quote: This Session lasts as long as the Network Connection.
requirements.condition: For a Session started with CleanSession set to 1
requirements.required_behavior: The Session lifetime must equal the lifetime of its Network Connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Session must not persist after that Network Connection ends.
requirements.why_checkable: The connection can be closed and Session existence checked immediately afterward and on a later connection.

requirements.quote: State data associated with this Session MUST NOT be reused in any subsequent Session [MQTT-3.1.2-6].
requirements.condition: After a Session created with CleanSession set to 1 has ended
requirements.required_behavior: Any subsequent Session must begin without reusing state data from the ended Session.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Client or Server must not reuse that state data in a subsequent Session.
requirements.why_checkable: Distinct successive Sessions can be instrumented to detect any carried-over subscriptions or in-flight message state.

requirements.quote:
The Session state in the Client consists of:
QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages which have been sent to the Server, but have not been completely acknowledged.
QoS 2 messages which have been received from the Server, but have not been completely acknowledged.
requirements.condition: When a QoS 1 message sent by the Client has not been completely acknowledged
requirements.required_behavior: The Client must retain that sent QoS 1 message in its Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: Client Session state can be inspected after pausing the QoS 1 acknowledgement flow.

requirements.quote:
The Session state in the Client consists of:
QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages which have been sent to the Server, but have not been completely acknowledged.
QoS 2 messages which have been received from the Server, but have not been completely acknowledged.
requirements.condition: When a QoS 2 message sent by the Client has not been completely acknowledged
requirements.required_behavior: The Client must retain that sent QoS 2 message in its Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: Client Session state can be inspected after pausing the outbound QoS 2 acknowledgement flow.

requirements.quote:
The Session state in the Client consists of:
QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages which have been sent to the Server, but have not been completely acknowledged.
QoS 2 messages which have been received from the Server, but have not been completely acknowledged.
requirements.condition: When a QoS 2 message received by the Client has not been completely acknowledged
requirements.required_behavior: The Client must retain that received QoS 2 message in its Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: Client Session state can be inspected after pausing the inbound QoS 2 acknowledgement flow.

requirements.quote:
The Session state in the Server consists of:
The existence of a Session, even if the rest of the Session state is empty.
The Client’s subscriptions.
QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages which have been sent to the Client, but have not been completely acknowledged.
QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages pending transmission to the Client.
QoS 2 messages which have been received from the Client, but have not been completely acknowledged.
Optionally, QoS 0 messages pending transmission to the Client.
requirements.condition: For every existing Server-side Session
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must retain the existence of the Session even when all other Session state is empty.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Server must not infer that no Session exists solely because the rest of its state is empty.
requirements.why_checkable: An empty Session can be created and its existence checked on a subsequent reconnect.

requirements.quote:
The Session state in the Server consists of:
The existence of a Session, even if the rest of the Session state is empty.
The Client’s subscriptions.
QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages which have been sent to the Client, but have not been completely acknowledged.
QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages pending transmission to the Client.
QoS 2 messages which have been received from the Client, but have not been completely acknowledged.
Optionally, QoS 0 messages pending transmission to the Client.
requirements.condition: When a Server-side Session has Client subscriptions
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must include the Client’s subscriptions in Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: Subscriptions can be created and the persisted Server Session state inspected or recovered on reconnect.

requirements.required_behavior: The Server must retain that sent QoS 1 message in Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: Server Session state can be inspected after pausing an outbound QoS 1 acknowledgement flow.

requirements.why_checkable: An implementation's optional QoS 0 persistence can be inspected to determine whether pending messages are represented as Session state.

requirements.quote: When CleanSession is set to 1 the Client and Server need not process the deletion of state atomically.
requirements.condition: When CleanSession is set to 1 and the Client or Server deletes prior Session state
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation is permitted to process deletion of that state non-atomically.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation that performs incremental state deletion can be checked without treating the lack of atomic deletion as a protocol violation.

requirements.quote: Retained messages do not form part of the Session state in the Server, they MUST NOT be deleted when the Session ends [MQTT-3.1.2.7].
requirements.condition: For retained messages held by the Server
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must maintain retained messages outside Client Session state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Retained messages must not be classified as part of a Client Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: A retained message can be published and storage ownership checked independently of Client Sessions.

requirements.quote: Retained messages do not form part of the Session state in the Server, they MUST NOT be deleted when the Session ends [MQTT-3.1.2.7].
requirements.condition: When a Client Session ends while the Server holds retained messages
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must preserve the retained messages after the Session ends.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Server must not delete retained messages merely because the Session ended.
requirements.why_checkable: A retained message can be created, a Session ended, and the retained message queried from a later Session.
